bull_bear.body:
- technology: global engineering capability via acquired technology and technical collaboration — evidence: acquisition of Continental Eagle Corporation (USA) and ongoing technical collaboration with CIRCOT support continuous product innovation
- distribution: new revenue vertical entry outside core cotton machinery — evidence: successful development and supply of Passenger Boarding Bridges (PBBs) enabled entry into the airport infrastructure segment [planned]
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Foreign exchange exposure — Exports contribute a significant share of revenue; fluctuations in foreign exchange rates can impact realisations, profitability and overall financial performance.
- Geopolitical and supply chain disruptions — Global operations expose the Company to risks from geopolitical tensions, trade restrictions, shipping disruptions and logistics bottlenecks that may affect timely execution of international orders.
- Technology disruption — Rapid advancements in engineering and manufacturing technologies require continuous investment in innovation and product development; failure to keep pace could affect long-term competitiveness.
- Dependence on cotton production — Demand for the Company's cotton processing machinery is closely linked to cotton production levels, which are influenced by climatic conditions, agricultural productivity and crop patterns; adverse weather or lower cotton output could impact industry demand.
- Raw material and commodity price volatility — Fluctuations in cotton prices, steel prices and other input costs, driven by global demand-supply dynamics and macroeconomic conditions, may exert pressure on margins and affect business performance.
- Export revenue concentration in Cotton Ginning Machinery segment — Overall performance was largely impacted by lower export revenues from the Cotton Ginning Machinery Segment (~60% of total revenue), caused by customer site unpreparedness and pending commercial clearances resulting in dispatch delays and deferred revenue recognition.
bull_bear.title: Bear — key risks

outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- The medium-term outlook for the Company remains positive, supported by sustained investments in infrastructure, manufacturing, renewable energy and industrial automation.
- Government initiatives such as Make in India, Atmanirbhar Bharat and continued capital expenditure on transportation, energy and industrial projects are expected to create strong demand across the Company's diversified engineering portfolio.
- Diversified business model provides resilience against sector-specific market cycles.
- Cotton Processing Machinery Division outlook supported by rising global cotton consumption, textile sector expansion and increasing investment in modern ginning infrastructure.
- PEB industry outlook favourable as infrastructure development, industrial expansion and logistics investments accelerate; well-integrated, technology-driven manufacturers with large fabrication capacities expected to be primary beneficiaries.
- Electric control panel demand supported by rising electricity demand, industrial automation, infrastructure expansion and renewable energy integration.
- Lower export revenues from the Cotton Ginning Machinery segment during the year were affected by customer site unpreparedness and pending commercial clearances, resulting in dispatch delays and deferred revenue recognition despite receipt of advances; domestic business registered healthy growth.
- Infrastructure segment witnessed healthy momentum, registering 30% YoY growth during the year.
- Cotton Processing Machinery Division: order book of ₹363 crores as of 31 March 2026.
- Pre-Engineered Buildings (PEB) Division: order book of ₹100 crore as of 31 March 2026, backed by a manufacturing capacity of 35,000 MTPA and over 600 completed projects.
- Electrical Panels Division: order book of ₹54 crore as of 31 March 2026.
